subject.title: Feature: Activity-aware run timeout (wall-clock timeout kills active multi-tool runs)

question: Should OpenClaw keep the current single wall-clock run timeout, adopt activity-aware idle timeout plus a hard cap in core, or limit this cleanup to the narrower linked subagent and timeout-notice fixes?
rationale: The current code can support a narrow patch, but the durable behavior affects core timeout semantics, config surface, resource caps, and message-delivery UX; automation should not choose that policy.

options.title: Adopt idle plus hard cap
options.body: Add an activity-aware idle deadline while retaining an absolute run ceiling and update config/docs/tests only with an explicit migration or compatibility plan.

options.title: Land narrow mitigations only
options.body: Review the linked subagent heartbeat and timeout-notice PRs without changing the global run-timeout model yet.

options.title: Keep wall-clock semantics
options.body: Treat the 48-hour default and explicit timeout override as the supported answer, and close the broader liveness request after documenting that policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt idle plus hard cap
recommendation.body: Add an activity-aware idle deadline while retaining an absolute run ceiling and update config/docs/tests only with an explicit migration or compatibility plan.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans current Gateway/agent runtime policy and config surface, and steipete is the strongest current-main routing signal from the relevant files.
